verbatim_locators.note: Coverage of this pass: Abstract, sections 1, 2, 4 and 5 and Table 1 read for one question (does any sourced index map mouse P1-P5 to a human age, and with what spread). Sections on neurogenesis, immune response, behaviour, and the figures were NOT read. Partial by design.

entries.proposition: One human age maps to two rodent ages far apart depending on the milestone: human term matches rat day 7.4 by GABA-synthesising enzyme level, and rat day 20.4 by choline acetyltransferase level (Romijn 1991, as reported by this review). A rodent-to-human age equivalence therefore carries no single number.
entries.snippet: A similar calculation to determine 16.2% of the adult rat levels corresponds to 7.4 days of age in the rat

entries.proposition: The second, much later mapping from the same paragraph.
entries.snippet: the relative levels of the choline acetyltransferase enzyme at birth compared with adulthood in humans was strikingly later, at pnd 20.4 in the rat cortex

entries.proposition: The review draws the conclusion itself: equating ages on one milestone may mislead.
entries.snippet: equating ages based upon a single milestone or event may lead to misinterpretation
entries.anchor: 4. Synaptogenesis and neurotransmission, Romijn paragraph, closing sentence

entries.proposition: The one sourced interval for the earliest postnatal days is white-matter based and already nine weeks wide: rodent days 1-3 map to 23-32 gestational weeks, day 7 to 32-36 weeks (Craig 2003, rats AND mice). So rodent P1-P5 sits at or before human term on this index; no index in the review places it after term.
entries.snippet: estimating that white matter development and axonal outgrowth in the rodent CNS at pnd 1–3 corresponds to 23–32 weeks gestation in human infants, while pnd 7 is analogous to 32–36 weeks

entries.proposition: Rat and mouse do not share even the neural-tube date, so a rat-anchored index is not automatically a mouse index.
entries.snippet: Neural tube formation occurs approximately mid-gestation in rodents, on gestational day (gd) 10.5–11 and 9–9.5 in rats and mice, respectively
